# Link Verifier — Sequential and Concurrent Crawling

Checking a website’s links one at a time leaves the caller waiting for each HTTP
response before checking the next URL. This exercise asks how to use that
waiting time to make progress on other independent checks. Compare the
sequential implementation with your own concurrent crawler that overlaps
blocking I/O while preserving the crawl’s behaviour and per-origin rate limit. A
reference solution is available after you have tried the exercise.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this example, attendees can:

- identify waiting for I/O in a sequential task and explain when independent
  work can proceed concurrently;
- implement concurrent checks while coordinating discovery and completion;
- distinguish the limit on checks in flight from the per-origin request rate;
- explain result visibility, interruption and executor shutdown; and
- interpret the report and explain why live-site timings and truncated crawl
  results are not a controlled performance comparison.

## Prerequisite

Install
[Oracle Java 25 JDK](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/) or
newer and make it available to `java` and `javac`. The Maven wrapper downloads
Maven and dependencies as needed; the walkthrough also needs network access to
the target site and its linked origins.

## The program to inspect

A simple crawler starts with a URL and maintains a queue of links to check. It
takes one URL at a time, fetches it and, when the response is an eligible HTML
page, extracts links to add to the queue. It continues until the queue is empty.
A limit bounds the number of distinct URLs admitted, and tracking those already
discovered prevents duplicate checks and cycles from keeping it busy.

`SequentialCrawler` follows this design: it waits for each request and processes
the result before checking another URL. While the request waits for I/O, other
already-discovered URLs remain unchecked.

```java
package demo;

import module java.base;
import module java.net.http;
import module org.jsoup;

import static demo.HttpResponses.isRedirect;

final class SequentialCrawler {

    private static final String USER_AGENT =
            "WorkshopLinkVerifier/1.0 (https://github.com/albertattard/workshop-java-concurrency)";

    CrawlResult crawl(final CrawlerConfiguration.Sequential configuration) throws InterruptedException {
        final URI start = configuration.start();
        final CrawlScope scope = new CrawlScope(start);
        final CrawlState state = new CrawlState(start, configuration.maxLinks());
        final CrawlResult.Builder result = CrawlResult.builder();
        final OriginRateLimiters limiters = new OriginRateLimiters(configuration.requestsPerSecond());

        try (HttpClient client = HttpClient.newBuilder().connectTimeout(configuration.connectTimeout()).build()) {
            while (state.hasPending()) {
                final URI url = state.removeNext();
                final HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(url)
                        .timeout(configuration.requestTimeout())
                        .header("User-Agent", USER_AGENT)
                        .GET()
                        .build();
                try {
                    if (Thread.interrupted()) {
                        throw new InterruptedException("Crawl interrupted before waiting for a request permit");
                    }

                    // Guava allows bursts after inactivity; this is not strict request spacing.
                    // Its wait is uninterruptible, so propagate interruption once it finishes.
                    limiters.forUrl(url).acquire();
                    if (Thread.interrupted()) {
                        throw new InterruptedException("Crawl interrupted while waiting for a request permit");
                    }

                    final HttpResponse<String> response = client.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString());
                    if (isRedirect(response)) {
                        final String location = response.headers().firstValue("Location").orElse("");
                        if (location.isBlank()) {
                            result.diagnostic("Missing redirect location: " + url);
                        } else {
                            try {
                                final URI target = Links.resource(url.resolve(location));
                                if (Links.isNotHttp(target)) {
                                    result.diagnostic("Unsupported redirect location on " + url + ": " + location);
                                } else {
                                    result.redirect(url, response.statusCode(), target);
                                    if (state.offer(target) == CrawlState.Admission.LIMIT_REACHED) {
                                        result.limitReached();
                                    }
                                    continue;
                                }
                            } catch (final IllegalArgumentException e) {
                                result.diagnostic("Invalid redirect location on " + url + ": " + location);
                            }
                        }
                        result.response(url, response.statusCode());
                        continue;
                    }

                    result.response(url, response.statusCode());
                    if (!shouldExtractLinks(url, response, scope)) {
                        continue;
                    }

                    for (final var element : Jsoup.parse(response.body(), url.toString()).select("a[href]")) {
                        try {
                            final URI link = Links.resource(url.resolve(element.attr("href")));
                            if (Links.isNotHttp(link)) {
                                continue;
                            }

                            if (state.offer(link) == CrawlState.Admission.LIMIT_REACHED) {
                                result.limitReached();
                            }
                        } catch (final IllegalArgumentException e) {
                            result.diagnostic("Invalid link on " + url + ": " + element.attr("href"));
                        }
                    }
                } catch (final IOException e) {
                    result.failure(url, e.toString());
                }
            }
        }

        return result.build();
    }

    private static boolean shouldExtractLinks(
            final URI url,
            final HttpResponse<?> response,
            final CrawlScope scope) {
        return response.statusCode() >= 200
                && response.statusCode() < 300
                && scope.contains(url)
                && response.headers().firstValue("Content-Type").orElse("")
                .toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)
                .startsWith("text/html");
    }
}
```

`CrawlState` owns the discovered URLs and pending queue.

```java
package demo;

import java.net.URI;
import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.Set;

import static java.util.Objects.requireNonNull;

/**
 * Tracks discovered URLs and the work still waiting to be checked.
 */
final class CrawlState {

    enum Admission {ADDED, ALREADY_DISCOVERED, LIMIT_REACHED}

    private final Set<URI> discovered = new HashSet<>();
    private final ArrayDeque<URI> pending = new ArrayDeque<>();
    private final int maxLinks;

    CrawlState(final int maxLinks) {
        if (maxLinks < 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Maximum number of links must be at least 1");
        }

        this.maxLinks = maxLinks;
    }

    CrawlState(final URI start, final int maxLinks) {
        this(maxLinks);
        offer(requireNonNull(start, "Start URI must not be null"));
    }

    Admission offer(final URI url) {
        requireNonNull(url, "url must not be null");
        if (discovered.contains(url)) {
            return Admission.ALREADY_DISCOVERED;
        }

        if (discovered.size() >= maxLinks) {
            return Admission.LIMIT_REACHED;
        }

        discovered.add(url);
        pending.add(url);

        return Admission.ADDED;
    }

    boolean hasPending() {
        return !pending.isEmpty();
    }

    URI removeNext() {
        return pending.remove();
    }
}
```

`ConcurrentCrawler` is the exercise. Implement `crawl` so that independent
checks can overlap, with at most the configured number of checks in flight.
Preserve the sequential crawler’s scope, deduplication, redirect and result
handling, URL limit, request timeouts and per-origin rate limit. Ensure the
crawl terminates after all discovered work is complete, handles interruption,
and shuts down its executor. The initial method throws
`UnsupportedOperationException` until you implement it.

Some pointers:

- Consider keeping discovery and the pending queue on one coordinator thread,
  with workers returning results and discovered links to it.
- An empty pending queue does not mean the crawl is finished while checks are
  still in flight. How will you collect completed checks and discover new work?
- `ExecutorCompletionService` can help collect results as tasks complete.
  Executor submission happens-before task actions, which happen-before the
  corresponding `Future.get()` returns. This makes the returned result visible;
  it does not order independent checks or guarantee a speedup.
- Distinguish the worker limit from the per-origin rate limit. Consider
  interruption while a worker waits for a permit or an HTTP response, and
  how the executor and HTTP client are closed.

```java
package demo;

import module com.google.common;
import module java.base;
import module java.net.http;
import module org.jsoup;

/**
 * Coordinates discovery on the calling thread; workers check one URL each.
 */
final class ConcurrentCrawler {

    private static final String USER_AGENT =
            "WorkshopLinkVerifier/1.0 (https://github.com/albertattard/workshop-java-concurrency)";

    CrawlResult crawl(final CrawlerConfiguration.Concurrent configuration) throws InterruptedException {
        throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not yet implemented");
    }
}
```

`OriginRateLimiters` supplies a shared Guava `RateLimiter` for each origin. A
worker can obtain a permit before sending a request. The configured rate
controls permits over time, whereas the worker count bounds checks in flight,
including checks waiting for permits. Bursts after inactivity are possible and
permits do not guarantee a minimum interval between actual request starts.

```java
package demo;

import com.google.common.util.concurrent.RateLimiter;

import java.net.URI;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Owned by one crawl and accessed only by its coordinator.
 */
final class OriginRateLimiters {

    private final Map<Origin, RateLimiter> limiters = new HashMap<>();
    private final double requestsPerSecond;

    OriginRateLimiters(final double requestsPerSecond) {
        this.requestsPerSecond = requestsPerSecond;
    }

    RateLimiter forUrl(final URI url) {
        return limiters.computeIfAbsent(Origin.of(url),
                origin -> RateLimiter.create(requestsPerSecond));
    }
}
```

`LinkVerifierCommand` selects the mode, reports outcomes sorted by URL and
prints elapsed crawl time. HTTP statuses, redirect targets and request failures
are reported separately. The URL-limit message means the crawl is incomplete; a
failure or timeout does not by itself prove a link is permanently broken.

```java
package demo;

import picocli.CommandLine.*;
import picocli.CommandLine.Model.CommandSpec;

import java.net.URI;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.concurrent.Callable;

@Command(name = "link-verifier", description = "Check website links.", showDefaultValues = true)
final class LinkVerifierCommand implements Callable<Integer> {

    private enum Mode {sequential, concurrent}

    @Parameters(index = "0", paramLabel = "URL", description = "Starting HTTP or HTTPS URL.")
    private URI start;

    @Option(names = "--mode", defaultValue = "sequential", paramLabel = "MODE", description = "Crawl mode: ${COMPLETION-CANDIDATES}.")
    private Mode mode;

    @Option(names = "--workers", defaultValue = "5", paramLabel = "COUNT", description = "Maximum concurrent checks.")
    private int workers;

    @Option(names = "--max-links", defaultValue = "100", paramLabel = "COUNT", description = "Maximum number of distinct URLs to check.")
    private int maxLinks;

    @Option(names = "--requests-per-second-per-origin", defaultValue = "5.0", paramLabel = "RATE", description = "Request rate per origin; bursts are possible after inactivity.")
    private double requestsPerSecond;

    @Option(names = "--connect-timeout", defaultValue = "PT5S", paramLabel = "DURATION", description = "Connection timeout as an ISO-8601 duration (e.g. PT5S).")
    private Duration connectTimeout;

    @Option(names = "--request-timeout", defaultValue = "PT10S", paramLabel = "DURATION", description = "Request timeout as an ISO-8601 duration (e.g. PT10S).")
    private Duration requestTimeout;

    @Option(names = {"-h", "--help"}, usageHelp = true, description = "Show this help message and exit.")
    private boolean helpRequested;

    @Spec
    private CommandSpec spec;

    CrawlerConfiguration configuration() {
        try {
            return switch (mode) {
                case sequential ->
                        new CrawlerConfiguration.Sequential(maxLinks, start, requestsPerSecond, connectTimeout, requestTimeout);
                case concurrent ->
                        new CrawlerConfiguration.Concurrent(maxLinks, start, requestsPerSecond, connectTimeout, requestTimeout, workers);
            };
        } catch (final IllegalArgumentException e) {
            throw new ParameterException(spec.commandLine(), e.getMessage(), e);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public Integer call() throws InterruptedException {
        final CrawlerConfiguration configuration = configuration();
        final CrawlResult result;
        final long started = System.nanoTime();
        try {
            result = switch (configuration) {
                case CrawlerConfiguration.Sequential sequential -> new SequentialCrawler().crawl(sequential);
                case CrawlerConfiguration.Concurrent concurrent -> new ConcurrentCrawler().crawl(concurrent);
            };
        } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw e;
        }
        final long elapsedNanos = System.nanoTime() - started;

        final var out = spec.commandLine().getOut();
        final var err = spec.commandLine().getErr();
        result.outcomes().stream()
                .sorted(Comparator.comparing(outcome -> outcome.url().toString()))
                .forEach(outcome -> {
                    switch (outcome) {
                        case CrawlResult.Response response -> out.println(response.status() + " " + response.url());
                        case CrawlResult.Redirect redirect -> {
                            out.println(redirect.status() + " " + redirect.url());
                            out.println("  -> " + redirect.target());
                        }
                        case CrawlResult.Failure failure ->
                                err.println("Failed " + failure.url() + ": " + failure.message());
                    }
                });
        result.diagnostics().forEach(err::println);
        if (result.limitReached()) {
            out.println("URL limit reached; results are incomplete");
        }
        out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "Crawl completed in %.3f s%n", elapsedNanos / 1_000_000_000.0);
        return 0;
    }
}
```

## Guided walkthrough

Run the following commands from `examples/link-verifier`. Both runs contact
`https://dev.java/` and URLs discovered on other origins.

1. Build the application and its runtime dependencies into `target/libs`.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

2. Run the sequential baseline. Sequential mode is the default.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path target/libs \
     --module demo.linkverifier \
     --max-links 100 \
     --requests-per-second-per-origin 10 \
     https://dev.java/
   ```

   One live-site run; URLs, statuses, failures and elapsed time can vary.

   ```
   301 http://www.oracle.com/javaone/index.html
     -> https://www.oracle.com/javaone/index.html
   403 https://bugs.java/
   200 https://dev.java/
   200 https://dev.java/assets/images/download/jdk-downloader.png
   ...
     -> https://www.youtube.com/java
   301 https://youtube.com/java/
     -> https://www.youtube.com/java
   URL limit reached; results are incomplete
   Crawl completed in 11.957 s
   ```

3. Implement `ConcurrentCrawler.crawl`. Use the sequential crawler and the
   pointers above as a starting point. The reference test is available at
   `solution/src/test/java/demo/ConcurrentCrawlerTest.java`; copy it to
   `src/test/java/demo/` to run it with `./mvnw test`. It checks crawl
   behaviour and overlapping independent requests.

4. When you are ready to compare your implementation with the reference
   solution, copy the solution and its tests into the project. This replaces
   your `ConcurrentCrawler.java`; save your work first if you want to keep it.

   ```shell
   rsync --archive solution/ ./
   ```

   Build the reference implementation and run its tests.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   Run the reference solution with two workers, using the same URL and rate
   limits as the sequential run.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path target/libs \
     --module demo.linkverifier \
     --mode concurrent \
     --workers 2 \
     --max-links 100 \
     --requests-per-second-per-origin 10 \
     https://dev.java/
   ```

   One live-site run; completion order and the resulting report can vary.

   ```
   301 http://www.oracle.com/javaone/index.html
     -> https://www.oracle.com/javaone/index.html
   403 https://bugs.java/
   200 https://dev.java/
   200 https://dev.java/assets/images/download/jdk-downloader.png
   ...
     -> https://www.youtube.com/java
   301 https://youtube.com/java/
     -> https://www.youtube.com/java
   URL limit reached; results are incomplete
   Crawl completed in 6.931 s
   ```

5. Compare the results from the sequential and concurrent runs.

   | Approach   | Workers | Rate limit per origin | 100-link limit |
   | ---------- | ------: | --------------------: | -------------: |
   | Sequential |       1 |            10 req/sec |     11.957 sec |
   | Concurrent |       2 |            10 req/sec |      6.931 sec |

   Compare the reported outcomes, the incomplete-crawl notice if present, and
   the elapsed times. Trace what happens when one request is waiting and another
   URL is already pending. Why might newly discovered links or a nearly empty
   queue leave fewer than two checks available?

   Two workers can overlap waits, but the rate limit, available work, server
   latency and other conditions also affect elapsed time. At the URL limit,
   different discovery order can select different URLs; the live site may also
   change between runs. These timings are observations, not a benchmark or a
   guaranteed speedup. For a controlled comparison, use an unchanged local
   fixture with enough capacity for concurrent requests and a limit high enough
   to include all its URLs.
